questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country where the locals spoke a language I understand, as I have experienced how unwilling a lot of Danes are to speak English with exchange students. Also, I wanted to go to England to explore the local culture and eat pies and other British comfort foods.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy. The only issue was that I went on my Master's, but the agreement UCPH has with Uni of Leeds wasn't properly made for that, so it was somewhat of a hassle to get the courses I needed to be allowed to go. 
Otherwise Uni of Leeds had lot of info about what to do at arrival and how to get the keys for accommodation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up by a cab paid for by the uni at the airport, brought to pick up my keys at one accom and then to my accom.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: When going on exchange, you are guaranteed student housing through uni. However, I get one of my lowest priorities which turned out okay, but had I known what I do now I would have gone private as there are many more and better options at lower prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You can rent a bike at The Bike Hub at Uni of Leeds for pretty cheap, which makes it so much easier to get to and from campus for lectures! However, do read the rules about biking and be brave, they are not as used to cyclists as we are here in CPH. 
Also, know that it'll be a different experience. I lived close to a forest and a park, which is really nice, but I also missed out on a lot of pubs/bars and their quizzes and stuff because it took like 30 ish mins to city centre.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You fill out a form using Microsoft with the courses you want to have. It is slightly confusing as the course in the UK is the entire academic program (e.g. bachelor's) and the module are the different subjects you have classes in. You look up the modules available for students from abroad and choose which ones you want in the order you prioritise them. You can't sort by semester, so it is a slight hassle to go through them all, but there's lots to choose from.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact your school (fakultet) and have them help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not much. I was not allowed to take modules at Master's level in other schools because they were already full, and ended up spending a lot of time asking individual lecturers whether I could have their module and if there was any space left. 
I ended up with 2/5 of the modules I wanted, but got the modules I needed to go.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't go here on your Master's if you can avoid it. 
Also, if you don't get assigned the modules you wanted I would email the professors and ask if they can manually add you, that might give you a better chance at getting the modules you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 15 ECTS Ma, 15 ECTS Ba

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar, most lectures and lab work. (I'm from school of Science)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Food Chemistry and Biochemistry (7,5 ECTS), Traditional and Alcoholic Beverages (5 ECTS), Leadership and Teams (5 ECTS), Functionality and Interactions of Components in Food 
Products (5 ECTS),  Nutritional Epidemiology and Dietary Research 
Methods (7,5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Traditional and Alcoholic Beverages because you brew your own beer, taste it and go to a brewery and it's just really fun. Also, a lot of internationals have it, so it's a great place to meet new people! 
Leadership and Teams is also really fun, it's a small class so you get to know everyone, and you go on a weekend trip in the middle of nowhere to do teambuilding exercises such as climbing in caves. My favourite module of them all!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was slightly less expensive (I went out to eat a few times a month, groceries were roughly 1200 per month). Housing is pretty expensive, I stayed in the cheapest possible student accommodation through uni.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Make sure to join at least one Society! I was in Nordic Society and Stitch and Bitch, and it was so nice to meet other people and to just have plans on weeknights

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basically everything. I think there's 100+ clubs with anything from religious to sports to country-specific to creative or gaming/board games. There's something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Nordic Society is nice if you wanna meet other people from Scandinavia. I also enjoyed Stitch and Bitch as it was nice to just knit/do something creative and chat with people. 
Also I know a lot of people enjoyed the movie club and the different sports clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Liverpool and York. Also, prioritise going to Scotland (especially Edinburgh) now that it's fairly close by. If going by train, buy a Railcard which gives you 1/3 off all train tickets and costs like 300dkk. If you wait till you arrive you can get a student discount on the Railcard using UniDays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy, it is fairly similar to DK. There's people from a lot of different cultures, but it's so fun to learn new stuff about people. 
Biggest difference is that beers are served in pints, which is pretty nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Driving in the left side of the road and learning to bike in the UK. Also saying "cheers" instead of thanks.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way you go out for 1-2 beers a few times a week, and that the beers are a lot cheaper than in DK. Also people are really kind and want to help if you have any issues.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
People are pretty young, so be prepared that your classmates are gonna be 18-20 years old. 
A lot of places have student discount, use it! 
Enjoy and go see all the stuff you want to. Don't wait for things to happen, plan them yourself and just invite people along.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're late with your assignments you can apply to get 7 more days before handing in without having to document why.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many great people and exploring the British culture with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The days you didn't have plans, as it can feel a little lonely in the beginning. However, just reach out to people even if you've only met them once, you're all in the same boat!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
